text: This lesson deploys a logical SQL server plus one database as code, with the database declared as the server's child using the same automatic-dependency pattern from Lesson 12.
A password never belongs in the file. A secure parameter tells Bicep never to log or output the value — it has to come from a Key Vault reference, an environment variable, or a CI/CD secret.
The mechanics are identical to deploying a Storage Account. What's different is the shape — a server-and-database pair instead of one resource on its own.
The CLI returning success is one signal. The Azure Portal's own deployment history is the second, independent confirmation the deployment actually succeeded.
A parent-child pair, a secret handled properly, confirmation from a second source. Next up: ARM templates versus Bicep.
